title: The Source Where Ice Becomes First Water

features.name: the thawing threshold
features.desc-on-touch: A tower of ice-forms begins here and descends—halfway through its height, the geometry softens, the structure becoming liquid, becoming flow. You watch it transition between states in a single form.

features.name: the first running
features.desc-on-touch: Water moves here for the first time—its path is uncertain, learning its own channel, repeating the river's work of finding the lowest place. You hear it as a sound becoming language.

features.name: the fence of becoming
features.desc-on-touch: A boundary marked by repeated forms—where ice ends and water begins, drawn in miniature. The fence itself is unclear about which side it belongs to.

features.name: the thaw-song
features.desc-on-touch: A sound rises here—the hum of transformation, ice learning it can move. The archive records it as a frequency that doesn't quite fit any single wavelength, caught between two states of matter.

features.name: the dawn-breaking
features.desc-on-touch: Light arrives here for the first time as ice retreats—you sense it as the moment when color begins to matter, when beauty becomes possible because things can now be reflected.

inscription: the source does not flow downward; it remembers falling from the sky and learning to go anywhere

file.name: Thaw_Sequence_Spring_Cycle_Northeast_Ridge.wav
file.note: A recording of ice becoming water—compressed frequencies at the threshold, sound caught between solid and liquid state, playing both ways at once.
